gap_text: Temporal and modal have no local execution, failure, cancellation, recovery or telemetry evidence. Their capabilities are untested, not failed.
next_check: Start `temporal server start-dev` in a new prefix and run a two-activity workflow on it. Test an activity failure with retry, cancellation, and a worker SIGKILL followed by restart, recording the event history and OTel spans. Record Modal as needing user login.

preregistration.expectation: temporal CLI 1.9.1 (checksum-verified download into the cache prefix) runs `temporal server start-dev` on loopback ports with a temp sqlite file; a Python temporalio worker runs a two-activity workflow. Expected: happy path completes; an activity that raises on attempt 1 is retried and succeeds on attempt 2 (history shows attempt 2); `temporal workflow cancel` ends the workflow Canceled; SIGKILL of the worker mid-activity followed by a new worker completes the workflow after the heartbeat timeout; the SDK TracingInterceptor exports spans to a local JSON file. Modal is recorded as needing user login: its client run with an empty temp HOME reports a missing token.
preregistration.criteria: Temporal arms pass iff each scenario's `temporal workflow show -o json` event history contains the expected terminal event (Completed, Completed with attempt 2 ActivityTaskStarted, Canceled, Completed after a timed-out attempt) and the span file contains workflow and activity spans. The gap's Modal clause cannot be closed without a user login, so the maximum outcome is advanced even if every Temporal arm passes.

limits: temporal server start-dev is the single-binary development server with sqlite; production persistence, multi-node history and upgrades are untested.
Workflow sandbox was disabled (UnsandboxedWorkflowRunner) to keep the harness in one file; determinism checks of the sandbox were not exercised.

The worker SIGKILL recovery relied on a 5 s heartbeat timeout and re-ran step1 from scratch (attempt 2 on a new pid); no heartbeat-details checkpoint was tested. The server itself was not killed mid-run; the restart check was a clean stop/start after all workflows finished.

Spans were exported with a SimpleSpanProcessor to local JSON-lines files, not to an OTel collector; the killed attempt's span is lost, so span data alone under-reports killed work while the event history keeps it (lastFailure "activity Heartbeat timeout").
Network: downloaded the 45,298,806-byte temporal CLI archive from GitHub releases and the temporalio, opentelemetry and modal wheels from PyPI; modal made no authenticated call.
Two runs (round 1 and fix round 2) on one WSL2 host with the same outcomes; loopback ports 17733/17734/17740; all processes were stopped.
remaining: Modal: execution, failure, cancellation, recovery and telemetry remain untested; they need a user Modal account login (`modal token new`), which this unit cannot perform. Temporal: covered locally on the dev server only (see limits).

fixround2_preregistration.label: fix round 2, written after the independent review and before the reruns
fixround2_preregistration.reason: Independent Codex review (codex exec --sandbox read-only --ephemeral, 2026-09-23) found: base64 Temporal payloads still carried the host home path; *.jsonl raw files were gitignored and so not committed; several provenance claims (checksum verification, archive size, modal version, fresh --require-hashes sync, installed versions) had no retained raw output; raw outputs lacked capture timestamps; and the Temporal harness hardcoded the second-worker launch delay as 3 s.
fixround2_preregistration.expectation: Rerun run_temporal.sh (UTC start/finish, measured second-worker launch delay, wall-clock kill time) in a new work dir and re-verify the archive checksum/size and record `modal --version` in a retained log. Expect the same scenario outcomes as the first run; the measured launch delay will exceed 3 s by the describe-call latency.
fixround2_preregistration.criteria: The rerun replaces the first run as cited evidence; outcomes that differ from the first run are reported. The Modal clause still caps the outcome at advanced.

review.findings_for_this_receipt: Finding 1: base64 payloads in the histories carried the host home path -> collector now decodes, sanitizes and re-encodes (6 files, 16 payloads); a decode-and-search probe finds none in the committed files and finds 3 in an unsanitized original (control). Finding 2: *.jsonl spans were gitignored -> committed as *.jsonl.txt. Finding 5: checksum/size/modal version lacked raw output -> raw/0-provenance-reverification.txt (post-hoc).
